records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:122,228 — the organizer email in the Google payload is always the main host's destinationCalendar[0].externalId even when creating on a secondary host's calendar via their credential, so the secondary host's event lists another user's calendar address as organizer
records.rationale: The diff shows GoogleCalendarService's createEvent destructures only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = calEventRaw?.destinationCalendar ...`) and uses its externalId as the organizer email, while the EventManager now loops over ALL destinationCalendar entries and calls createEvent per destination credential (`for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`). For a secondary host's destination, the organizer email still comes from destinationCalendar[0], which belongs to a different host/calendar — a genuine mismatched-organizer defect introduced by this change.

records.rationale: The diff shows Google createEvent now selects via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, so a destination calendar whose credentialId is null/absent (legacy rows) or one passed a non-matching credentialId falls back to 'primary', creating the event on the wrong calendar. records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:727-760 — the rewritten loadUsers throws a plain Error for an empty dynamicUserList (mapped to a 500 instead of 400) and re-throws all HttpErrors (e.g. 404) as 400, discarding original error detail
records.rationale: The rewritten loadUsers in the diff throws plain `new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` for an empty list; the catch only re-throws HttpError/PrismaClientKnownRequestError as 400 and otherwise throws `HttpError({ statusCode: 500 })`, so the empty-list case yields 500 instead of a 400. Also, any pre-existing HttpError (e.g. 404) is caught and re-thrown as a new 400 HttpError, losing the original status code. Both mechanisms are directly visible in the diff hunk and describe changed error-handling behavior introduced by this change.
